sol.problem:
The parser strips an optional fn prefix and then independently permits every function kind. Consequently it accepts bare cc/r headers and fn oracle/action/perm_action headers, which are outside the normative grammar. This is executable admission, not a harmless diagnostic spelling: with no arguments and --budget 1, run-cc reports COMPLETED, results=[], steps=1; hash/check both exit 0. Exact LF-terminated witness:
bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32

section symbols
{"0":{"interface_hash":"2060222c2773451dd9a97e146d566bfca81c7a91c7fe04bd90d7e841163f531e","kind":"cc","name":"a","signature":{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":[],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}}}

section functions
cc @a () () () () ()
^entry():
ret
The independent interface=closure hash is 2060222c2773451dd9a97e146d566bfca81c7a91c7fe04bd90d7e841163f531e and object_hash is b6f4dc99c6f84d162c82c54ea4c41ceee3e9d4cc09a00c3ab8bd80d282faec3f. I also reproduced acceptance of bare r and fn-prefixed oracle/action/perm_action as the first definition. is_head recognizes only normative prefixes, so the admission is additionally inconsistent with function position.

Preserve the exact five parameter lists and validate before constructing the Function. The determining §16.2 production is quoted exactly: fhead := ("fn" SP ("cc"|"r") | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc") SP "@" NAME ... . There is no optional fn alternative. Expected behavior for the witness is Object::parse Err citing §16.2, and CLI hash/check/run-cc exit 1 with empty stdout and that diagnostic, before executing ret. Add the CLI counterpart with run-cc a --budget 1 and no inputs. Test bare r plus fn-prefixed oracle/action/perm_action/lproc as first definitions and require rejection when placed after another valid definition as well. Recompute the stored interface hash independently as SHA-256 of isa=0.8 LF ptr_width=32 LF canonical signature LF exact mutated function LF. The resulting interface=closure hashes are respectively 607bffa4376f76dc181141c19dc70dfbde0d8064e3d220187b13001e25cab0ca, 31e7ad0837d13f0cd78e0fc2a155016c006ab18e3ecf6cc367308d58eb274437 and a2f5278ca8db3abb0e407e475c1fba93c4307b97f0db8c1fe4a0bbe2b48da782. Their object hashes are 3868eb11e0293db6f43d3a9c5589c36feab4d88916327a34241141c1949b2dd6, 6e0b6cfb1a74f8974706264ddc3b762bda7226e0abeb284f97978d5cb2f7d4f3 and 4ede077a7344efa101b22cd0f990feacde2c1a415dbec6667ee61290f9747480. All three actually pass check with status ok and execute inc8(255), B=3 as {code:0,payload:0,steps:3}; all should be load errors. codex.fix: Change src/object.rs::Object::parse_functions to parse exactly the fhead alternatives, and use the same header recognizer for function-boundary detection in is_head. The determining §16.2 text is fhead := ("fn" SP ("cc"|"r") | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc") ...; therefore fn oracle/fn action/fn perm_action/fn lproc and bare cc/r MUST reject. In parse_functions, reject an empty list when the bounds clause is present: the production says (SP "bounds" SP "{" INT ("," SP INT)* "}")?, requiring at least one INT. An action with no loops can omit the clause; this does not forbid its empty signature bounds array. In instruction, use a nonempty LHS parser: §16.2 says lhs := NAME | "(" NAME ("," SP NAME)* ")", whereas the operand-list production permits empty lists. Reject () = even for zero-result instructions. Add tests/parser.rs::r10_exact_fhead_and_nonempty_optional_productions asserting Object::parse errors citing §16.2 for each literal mutation above; these assertions fail today. Include bare cc/r as the first and later function and every invalid fn-prefixed Q kind, so boundary detection is not position-dependent. Keep positive controls for canonical fn cc/fn r/Q headers, omitted bounds, regs {  } bounds {1} on a one-trip action, ordinary nonempty tuple LHS and legal empty operand lists. Add CLI check/hash tests using the supplied mutated pins: expected exit 1, empty stdout, §16.2 stderr regardless of input or budget; no execution should occur. These are explicit grammar rules, not an ambiguity requiring a SPEC-QUESTIONS exception.

codex.problem:
Inverse recognition confuses the ordered lexical predicate stack with the semantic effective-control set. Start from tests/fixtures/r9-codex-oracle.bisa: keep @o, set @a signature in to [1,1], and replace @a with the following exact LF-terminated function:
action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in, q:wire in) () (tk:token) ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
d = qalloc any 1
f = qalloc any 4
h c
qpred p
qpred q
oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()
qunpred q
qunpred p
qpred q
qpred p
oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()
qunpred p
qunpred q
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree f
qfree d
qfree c
The independent @a interface=closure hash is 386dce74595f0e05ed2b7eb9218fc22fece3fafe7ad6fd206aed542ad8b7deef; @o remains cab76c914fa09a3fc8237381c6de91e83eeaefbd65cb7f52571ed4020abe8926. With canonical stored-H symbols and the original standard header/section formatting, object_hash is 7b1153bae80cc041447870eaa9623f73e6cb6df5085365a1efcbac99789076ad. Actual hash/check: exit 1, empty stdout, §6.2: released value has not been uncomputed. Removing only the borrow/CX/return triplet still rejects. Making both call contexts push p then q passes. A second independently tested variant with first stack [p] and second stack [p,p] also rejects. Hand: both calls are controlled by p AND q in the first witness (by p in the duplicate variant). At B=1 each toggles d by p*q*c, leaving f=0; at B=0 each toggles the same fault bit by p*q. Each pair is identity, H H restores c=0, CX(0,b) is identity for every borrowed b/reference R, and all workspace is zero at release. Thus the whole action is identity on t,p,q and bR. validation.rs embeds s.predicates in its oracle version and again in change/joint_change keys, so equal sets do not cancel. borrow.rs also compares Node.controls as ordered vectors (and direct qpred can retain duplicates), so repairing only the first validator is insufficient.
codex.fix: Keep the lexical predicate stack for push/pop validation, but introduce a canonical semantic effective-control representation for operation identities: resolve scalar physical wires, retain each polarity, sort and deduplicate equal literals, and retain the complete current version/dependency snapshots. Apply it to validation.rs::Object::validate_action_sequence oracle/action keys, Discipline::change/joint_change and other context-bearing keys, and to borrow.rs Compiler/Node construction and instantiation before Facts::reversible compares events. Do not sort input/output ABI operands or discard token/callee/version identity, negative polarities, or all-operand LIFO requirements. The determining §2 sentence defines effective control context as "the set of wires on the active predicate stack plus the inherited control context" and says "duplicates count once". §3.5 says "the active predicate is their conjunction"; §5.2 says "The oracle is an involution on (ins, tgt, fr) and its own adjoint"; §4.7 says "adj oracle_call … ≡ oracle_call …". Consequently [p,q] and [q,p], and [p] and [p,p], denote identical controls for this exact inverse, not different operations. Add tests/r1_borrow.rs::r10_equivalent_control_sets_preserve_opaque_inverse with the exact pinned object above and the duplicate variant. Object::parse success fails now. After the fix require parse/check/hash success; run-action a --mut 0 --in 1,1 --arg token:1,0,0,0 must return unchanged state {"011":[1,0]}, wires=3; token:0,0,0,0 has the same result. Independently initialize forward and adjoint across all t,p,q basis inputs and a superposition of controls; supply borrowed b entangled with untouched R and require exact identity and no escaping workspace. Require reverse equals_entry=true. Add nested qloop 1 / local-call variants, plus negative controls where one predicate is absent, has opposite polarity, changes version, or the token differs: those must not gain spurious cancellation. Extend the same effective-set test to qinplace explicit swapped g/ginv keys. No certificate, budget cap or extra syntactic restriction is justified.
